title: the siege
hook: two spies dressed as monkeys are caught in Rama's camp, and he lets them go

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vibhishana's crossing. Rama vowed safety to anyone who comes even once and says I am yours, and crowned Vibhishana on the beach. Even if it were Ravana.

The army crosses the bridge and spreads out along Lanka's shore. Across the island, Ravana does what any general would. He sends two of his ministers, Shuka and Sarana, to count the enemy. They take the shape of monkeys and slip in among the troops. It almost works. But one person in that camp knows exactly what a rakshasa in disguise looks like, because he grew up among them. Vibhishana sees through them, and they're dragged before Rama.
screen: `THE ARMY IS ACROSS.` → `TWO SPIES DRESSED AS MONKEYS.` → `VIBHISHANA SEES THROUGH THEM.`

segments.voice: In a war story, you know what usually happens to caught spies, and the monkeys are ready to do it. The two rakshasas, terrified, confess: Ravana sent us to count your army. And Rama laughs. If you've seen everything, he says, go back. If there's anything you missed, look again; Vibhishana will show you around. You're unarmed and you were caught. You won't be killed. Then he gives them a message. Tell Ravana: show me the strength you relied on when you carried Sita away. Tomorrow he'll see my arrows fall on his city. The spies go home and tell Ravana the truth, the last thing he wants to hear. Valmiki then gives a long scene on a high tower. Ravana looks out over the enemy camp, and Sarana points out the leaders one by one: Nila, Angada, Nala, Hanuman, Jambavan, Sugriva, Rama and Lakshmana. Their advice, after all that, is to make peace and return Sita. Ravana is furious and throws them out. A siege is a contest of fear. Ravana wanted information, and Rama gave him more than he asked for, so he'd know exactly what was coming. Mercy and confidence arrive together. And the spies who came to count soldiers go home telling their king to make peace.
screen: `CAUGHT SPIES, AND A LAUGH.` · `LOOK AGAIN, THEN GO HOME.` · `THE LEADERS NAMED FROM A TOWER.` · `MERCY AND CONFIDENCE TOGETHER.` · then, large: `THEY CAME TO COUNT AND WENT HOME TO WARN.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who seems to be measuring you, and picture Rama's open hand: no tricks, nothing hidden. Rest for a few slow breaths in that steadiness, with nothing to guard and nothing to prove.
The siege. It begins with two spies caught and set free, carrying a message: Rama is here, he hides nothing, and he's coming.
Your line: nothing to hide. Next comes one last offer at the gates. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Storytellers often use the release of Shuka and Sarana to show the code of war in the Ramayana: an unarmed messenger or captive is not killed.

fork.setup: you're Rama. two of Ravana's spies have just been caught in your camp. what do you do?
options: let them look around, then send them home with a message.
put them to death as a warning.
fork.reveal: he lets them see whatever they missed, and sends them back to tell Ravana to show the strength he used to take Sita.

original.note: Sanskrit Laṅkā: Ravana's island city; in Valmiki it is a golden city on a mountain, Trikuta.

trapdoor: what you thought: the siege began with an attack.
what it means: it began with spies caught and released, and a message: show me your strength.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki gives a whole catalog of the monkey leaders, named one by one from Ravana's tower.

chat.says: Why did Rama let Ravana's spies go home instead of punishing them?
options: They were unarmed and caught, and he wanted Ravana to see what was coming.
He hoped the spies would switch sides and fight for him inside Lanka.
He didn't know they were spies until after they had left his camp.
chat.meaning: Rama spares unarmed, captured spies and shows them everything. Mercy and confidence together send them home urging peace.

Shuka.meaning: one of Ravana's ministers, sent to spy on Rama's army

Sarana.meaning: Ravana's minister who names Rama's leaders from the tower

rakshasa.meaning: one of Ravana's people in the epic, able to change shape

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's brother, who came over to Rama's side

Lanka.meaning: Ravana's island city across the sea

recall: the old vulture king who fought Ravana
an old measure of distance, many miles

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 25 (Shuka and Sarana caught and released)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 26–29 (the leaders named from Ravana's tower; the spies' advice; Ravana's anger)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Rama's message to Ravana through the spies: paraphrased; confirm.
The list of leaders named from the tower is shortened; confirm those named are in Sarana's catalog.
In some versions it is Shuka who makes the main report; the script gives the naming to Sarana.
The scene where Ravana shows Sita a magic head of Rama (Yuddha 31–33) and Sarama comforts her is left out of this run for length; a Keeper may want it placed somewhere.
